html:
UE 5.6 alpha.4 transfer names and destination

The engine-wide ForgeMCP plugin is 0.2.13-alpha.4 (descriptor version 19) for UE 5.6.1 Win64. The external MCP server source is 0.3.10.

Blender-to-Unreal transfers use /Game/Content/Returns/ as the default destination folder. ForgeMCP appends the exact Blender source object name to that folder, without an SM_ prefix, generated replacement name, or numeric suffix. The preview shows the final asset path. If that exact path already exists, the workflow returns destination_exists; it never invents another name. The apply step rechecks the destination before export. If a source name cannot be used as a valid Unreal package name, the workflow asks for the source to be renamed instead of silently changing it.

Unreal-to-Blender continues to leave the optional Blender object-name override blank by default. The source Unreal asset name is retained. The field label now states that it is an optional override. The import button reads Send to Unreal (from Blender), and the destination field is labeled as a folder.

Validation

  • The UE 5.6.1 isolated host compiled both plugin modules and completed its 28-action UnrealEditor target build successfully.
  • The 50-file alpha archive passed package integrity checks and loaded in a clean Blueprint-only project with real stdio MCP discovery. The engine-wide package verification also passed, loaded the exact DLL from the Marketplace plugin folder, and reported health version 0.2.13-alpha.4.
  • Archive: Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Unreal-Alpha-0.2.13-alpha.4-UE5.6.1-Win64.zip, SHA-256 814c8c6bf87d6a4f6d2709525d252f497090df9e9643cab785f91b3ad05a3823.
  • The engine-wide installer updated the plugin and retained alpha.3 at Engine/Saved/ForgeMCPInstallBackups/0966d6d9a60444d0a10cbe2942ba3f09/MajesticForge. It did not modify project files.
  • Python regression suite: 345 passed. Ruff, Python source compilation, pip check, and git diff --check passed.

At verification time, no Unreal or Blender bridge sessions were connected. The disposable editor/package checks validate the compiled plugin and MCP contract; the changed panel has not yet been visually inspected inside the user's project, and no real two-application transfer was applied. The Blender scene and project assets were not modified during acceptance.
